name: Rails + Hotwire + PostgreSQL
choose_when: An integrated monolith and server-owned UI fit the product.
A small team benefits from stable conventions and limited integration work.
avoid_when: The core is an offline-first canvas or requires extensive browser-owned state.
Hard CPU/latency constraints justify a specialist service.

tools.alternatives: React client when browser-owned state dominates; retain Rails API
tools.reason: Server-rendered HTML and selective JavaScript limit duplicated UI state.
tools.limits: Do not force Hotwire onto rich offline editors.

tools.alternatives: SQLite for deliberately single-host deployments
tools.reason: Relational constraints and conventional migrations fit business data.
tools.limits: Use unique/foreign-key constraints; assess locks and use expand/contract changes for rolling deploys.

tools.alternatives: Devise when its additional authentication modules are needed
tools.reason: Generated local sessions plus explicit per-resource authorization.
tools.limits: Generator is a starting point; signup, authorization and account lifecycle require product decisions.

tools.alternatives: Existing resource-level policy implementation; keep authentication separate
tools.reason: Generated local sessions plus explicit per-resource authorization.
tools.limits: Generator is a starting point; signup, authorization and account lifecycle require product decisions.

tools.alternatives: Another Active Job backend only for measured operational needs
tools.reason: Database-backed jobs avoid a mandatory separate broker.
tools.limits: Configure worker capacity, retry limits and idempotency; separate queue DB does not guarantee atomic app-write/enqueue.

tools.alternatives: Keep RSpec in an established RSpec repository
tools.reason: Exercise authorization, database constraints and essential browser flows.
tools.limits: Browser tests need their driver/browser; unit tests alone miss UI and transaction races.

tools.alternatives: Preserve existing compatible project tooling
tools.reason: Style, application scanning and dependency advisories cover different risks.
tools.limits: Scans do not establish security; test tenant isolation and unsafe uploads. bundler-audit has GPL-3.0 licensing.

tools.alternatives: Managed container hosting when server operations are undesirable
tools.reason: Portable container deployment with application-owned configuration.
tools.limits: Requires registry/server credentials and persistent data strategy; backups and restore drills remain operator work.

tools.default: Generators + routes/schema/test feedback + version-matched Rails guides
tools.alternatives: Add only a reviewed MCP integration with a concrete need
tools.reason: Conventions make edits easier to locate and verify.
tools.limits: Agent productivity is an inference; no cross-framework coding-success benchmark established.

tools.alternatives: Paid infrastructure/support when operationally useful
tools.reason: No mandatory proprietary Rails hosting service.
tools.limits: Dependency licenses remain separate; do not infer all gems are MIT.

alternatives: Preserve an existing compatible project choice
tools.reason: Framework mailers integrate templates and queued delivery
tools.limits: Configure provider transport and sender; use deliver_later when delivery must be queued; test content and failure behavior. Provider acceptance is not inbox delivery.

alternatives: Preserve an existing compatible project choice
tools.reason: Framework attachments support external storage and direct uploads
tools.limits: Run the installed-version Active Storage generator/migrations; configure private storage, authorization, limits and cleanup. Public blob URLs and user-supplied files need an explicit access policy.

alternatives: Preserve an existing compatible project choice
tools.reason: Rails channels integrate WebSocket messages with application code
tools.limits: Configure chosen cable adapter and connection/channel authorization; test reconnect, revoked membership and host proxy behavior. Broadcast is not durable event history.

setup_steps: Start in a source directory in a local development workspace with supported Ruby/Rails, PostgreSQL and Git installed; choose and record compatible versions before generation.
Run rails new product -d postgresql; enter product; configure development/test database access without committing credentials.
Run bin/rails generate authentication; add Pundit via bundle add pundit and run bin/rails generate pundit:install; implement signup and resource policies deliberately.
Run bin/rails db:prepare; start bin/rails server. Configure Solid Queue from the installed-version guide and run its worker with bin/jobs when enabled.
Add bundler-audit to the development group if absent; preserve Gemfile.lock. Define authorization, duplicate-job and migration tests.
Prepare config/deploy.yml, secrets, database persistence and backup/restore procedure. Only in an authorized deployment run bundle exec kamal setup initially or bundle exec kamal deploy thereafter.
open_questions: Which signup, SSO/MFA and resource authorization policies are required?
Does the product fit server-owned screens or need substantial offline/client state?
Which host, mail/storage services, worker throughput and restore requirements apply?

name: Laravel + Livewire + PostgreSQL
choose_when: PHP team or Laravel ecosystem fit is strong.
Integrated auth, queues and concrete agent inspection tools reduce assembly work.
avoid_when: The UI fundamentally requires an offline/client-state architecture; use the Inertia alternative if Laravel still fits.
A hosting plan cannot operate needed queue workers or scheduled jobs.

tools.alternatives: Official React/Vue/Svelte Inertia kits for heavier client interactions
tools.reason: One supported starter establishes coherent UI/auth integration.
tools.limits: Starter includes Flux; distinguish its free components from paid Pro assets.

tools.alternatives: SQLite for local/small deployments; existing MySQL where operationally established
tools.reason: Conventional ORM and migrations with a production relational store.
tools.limits: Use constraints; production-engine integration tests; never use migrate:fresh against retained data.

tools.alternatives: WorkOS starter variant for managed identity requirements
tools.reason: Existing authentication flow plus resource-level authorization.
tools.limits: Policies remain application work; managed identity adds external terms/cost.

tools.alternatives: Existing explicit resource-level authorization implementation; identity providers still require policies
tools.reason: Existing authentication flow plus resource-level authorization.
tools.limits: Policies remain application work; managed identity adds external terms/cost.

tools.alternatives: Redis + Horizon for queue dashboards/balancing; SQS for an established managed queue
tools.reason: Simple starting infrastructure with explicit scale-up options.
tools.limits: Use after-commit dispatch, idempotent jobs, finite retries and worker restarts. Horizon requires Redis.

tools.default: Pest or PHPUnit from starter; Dusk for key browser flows
tools.alternatives: Keep the existing test runner rather than changing syntax for its own sake
tools.reason: Application and browser verification complement each other.
tools.limits: Use a dedicated test database and install Dusk only in development.

tools.alternatives: Existing equivalent tooling if already maintained
tools.reason: Formatting, static checks and dependency advisory checks expose different failures.
tools.limits: Install a compatible Larastan version and configure its extension; no audit substitutes for authorization tests.

tools.default: PHP-FPM web service + worker supervisor + scheduler on chosen host
tools.alternatives: Laravel Cloud for managed operation; Forge for server management
tools.reason: A conventional process model is a practical default.
tools.limits: Serve only public/; APP_DEBUG=false; persist uploads; reload workers after releases; paid platforms are optional.

tools.alternatives: Normal CLI/docs when MCP is unavailable
tools.reason: Version-aware documentation and route/schema/log inspection provide concrete context.
tools.limits: Tools can execute application code; use development credentials and honor maintained repository instructions. A README-only integration is an optional project policy; inspect installed Boost help before opting out of generated instructions.

tools.alternatives: Optional paid Flux Pro and managed services
tools.reason: Framework use does not mandate a hosting subscription.
tools.limits: Check each optional asset/package/service license separately.

alternatives: Preserve an existing compatible project choice
tools.reason: Mailables and queue integration keep delivery in application conventions
tools.limits: Configure the selected mailer and verified sender; use queued mail where required, after-commit handling and failed-job monitoring. Provider acceptance is not inbox delivery.

alternatives: Preserve an existing compatible project choice
tools.reason: Storage disks support private local or S3-backed files
tools.limits: Configure filesystems.php; install the selected adapter only, authorize downloads and uploads, define size/type limits and retention. Ephemeral deploy disks are not durable shared storage.

tools.default: Laravel broadcasting + Reverb when self-hosted sockets are required
alternatives: Preserve an existing compatible project choice
tools.reason: Private channels integrate realtime application events
tools.limits: Use the installed broadcasting setup; configure Echo, channel authorization, queued events and a supervised Reverb process. Verify TLS/proxy/scaling and reconnect; broadcast is not durable replay.

setup_steps: Start in a local development workspace with a supported PHP/Composer runtime, PostgreSQL, Node/npm and Git. Resolve actual package compatibility; Boost minimums do not define Laravel minimums.
Install installer if needed with composer global require laravel/installer; run laravel new product and choose Livewire, PostgreSQL and the desired test runner; enter product.
Configure .env database/mail/queue settings and confirm application key generation; do not commit secrets. Run php artisan migrate against the intended development database.
Run npm install then npm run build; run composer run dev. Configure a supervised queue worker and scheduler separately for production.

Add composer require laravel/boost --dev; inspect installed boost:install help and configure the selected integration. Honor generated guidance unless the repository explicitly chooses README-only instructions; inspect available installer options or configure MCP manually for that policy.
Add compatible Larastan as a dev dependency and configure phpstan.neon using its guide. For browser tests add laravel/dusk as a dev dependency then run php artisan dusk:install.

Prepare an authorized release: install locked production dependencies, build assets, review migrations, run php artisan optimize, and reload supervised services. Confirm backup/restore and rollback compatibility before production migration.
open_questions: Which starter-kit features and paid UI components are actually required?
Which identity and per-resource authorization policies must be supported?
Which host, mail/storage providers, realtime capacity and worker/scheduler operation will own production?
